'''Yitzhak Mastai''' ({{Langx|he|יצחק מסתאי}}) is a [[chemistry]] professor at [[Bar Ilan University]], specializing in [[Chirality#Chemistry|chirality]] at the [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoscale]] and in [[nanotechnology]].

==Biography==
Mastai<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://research.biu.ac.il/content/prof-mastais-lab |title=Prof. Mastai, Bar-Ilan University Research Authority |access-date=2018-05-26 |archive-date=2018-05-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527032009/http://research.biu.ac.il/content/prof-mastais-lab |url-status=dead }}</ref> was born in 1966 in [[Tel Aviv|Tel Aviv-Yafo]]. He obtained his B.Sc. in [[physical chemistry]] from [[Bar-Ilan University]] in 1989, and in 1999, received his PhD from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] under the supervision of Prof. [[Gary Hodes]] on [[Nanomaterials|Nanomaterial]] [[Chemical synthesis|Synthesis]]. He then spent three years as a post-doctoral Fellow at the [[Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces|Max Planck Institute]] of [[Interface and colloid science|Colloids and Interfaces]], working with both Prof. [[:de:Markus Antonietti|Markus Antonietti]] and Prof. Helmut Cölfen on [[Biomimetic synthesis|Biomimetic Chemistry]] and [[Chirality (chemistry)|Chiral]] [[Polymer]]s. In 2003 he joined the staff of the Chemistry Department at Bar Ilan, where he currently holds the position of a Professor of [[Nanotechnology]] and Chemistry, leading the Chirality Nanoscale laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ch.biu.ac.il/mastai |title=Prof. Mastai's Lab - Chemistry Department, Bar-Ilan University |access-date=2018-05-26 |archive-date=2018-05-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527201712/http://ch.biu.ac.il/mastai |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Mastai is married to [[Dina von Schwarze-Mastai]], a senior [[Psychologist#Clinical psychologists|clinical psychologist]] and a distinguished [[Translation#Literary translation|translator]] of German-Hebrew [[poetry]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0AS0swEACAAJ&q=Dina+von+Schwarze-Mastai |editor=Dina von Schwarze-Mastai |editor2=Aurélie Maurin |editor3=Tziona Shamay |date=2016 |title=Beyond border: Hebrew-German poetry}}</ref> Dina and Yitzhak have three children.

==Scientific interests and publications==
Mastai's earlier interests included [[Nanomaterials#Synthesis|nanomaterial synthesis]]<ref>Avivi, S.; Mastai, Y.; Hodes, G.; Gedanken, A., Sonochemical hydrolysis of Ga3+ ions: Synthesis of scroll-like cylindrical nanoparticles of gallium oxide hydroxide. Journal of the American Chemical Society 1999, 121, (17), 4196-4199.</ref>
especially [[Sonoelectrochemistry|Sono (electro)]],<ref>Mastai, Y.; Polsky, R.; Koltypin, Y.; Gedanken, A.; Hodes, G., Pulsed sonoelectrochemical synthesis of cadmium selenide nanoparticles. Journal of the American Chemical Society 1999, 121, (43), 10047-10052.</ref> the [[Chemical synthesis|Chemical Synthesis]] of [[Semiconductor]]s and Fullerene-like Nanoparticles,<ref>Avivi, S.; Mastai, Y.; Gedanken, A., A new fullerene-like inorganic compound fabricated by the sonolysis of an aqueous solution of TlCl3. Journal of the American Chemical Society 2000, 122, (18), 4331-4334.</ref> and [[Nanomaterials#Characterization|Nanomaterial characterization]].<ref>Antonietti, M.; [[Katharina Landfester|Landfester, K.]]; Mastai, Y., The vision of "Nanochemistry", or is there a promise for specific chemical reactions in nano-restricted environments? Israel Journal of Chemistry 2001, 41, (1), 1-5</ref><ref>Homyonfer, M.; Mastai, Y.; Hershfinkel, M.; Volterra, V.; Hutchison, J. L.; Tenne, R., Scanning tunneling microscope induced crystallization of fullerene-like MoS2. Journal of the American Chemical Society 1996, 118, (33), 7804-7808.</ref><ref>Mastai, Y.; Polarz, S.; Antonietti, M., Silica-carbon nanocomposites: A new concept for the design of solar absorbers. Advanced Functional Materials 2002, 12, (3), 197-202.</ref>
His current research focuses on Nanoscale Chirality,<ref>Mastai, Y., Enantioselective crystallization on nanochiral surfaces. Chemical Society Reviews 2009, 38, (3), 772-780.</ref><ref>Mastai, Y.; Volkel, A.; Colfen, H., Separation of racemate from excess enantiomer of chiral nonracemic compounds via density gradient ultracentrifugation. Journal of the American Chemical Society 2008, 130, (8), 2426-2427.</ref><ref>Lidor-Shalev, O.; Pliatsikas, N.; Carmiel, Y.; Patsalas, P.; Mastai, Y., Chiral Metal-Oxide Nanofilms by Cellulose Template Using Atomic Layer Deposition Process. ACS Nano 11, (5), 4753-4759.</ref> Synthesis and Analysis of Chiral Nanosurfaces, Chiral [[Self-assembled monolayer|self-assembled Monolayers]] (SAM), and Polymeric Chiral Nanoparticles.<ref>Medina, D. D.; Goldshtein, J.; Margel, S.; Mastai, Y., Enantioselective crystallization on chiral polymeric microspheres. Advanced Functional Materials 2007, 17, (6), 944-950.</ref><ref>Preiss, L. C.; Werber, L.; Fischer, V.; Hanif, S.; Landfester, K.; Mastai, Y.; Munoz-Espi, R., Amino-Acid-Based Chiral Nanoparticles for Enantioselective Crystallization. Advanced Materials 27, (17), 2728.</ref> Mastai and his colleagues, have gained international reputation in these fields, and have pioneered several new concepts and techniques in the following areas: (1) SAM's for the preparation of Chiral Nanosurfaces for Chiral resolution by [[crystallization]]. (2) Chiral ordered [[Mesoporous silica]] by Chiral polymer -[[Template reaction|Templated]] Synthesis. (3) An innovative new Carbon Chiral Mesoporous, based on the [[Carbonization]] of Chiral [[Ionic liquids]].<ref>Fuchs, I.; Fechler, N.; Antonietti, M.; Mastai, Y., Enantioselective Nanoporous Carbon Based on Chiral Ionic Liquids. Angewandte Chemie-International Edition 55, (1), 408-412.</ref> (4) The development of [[Near-field scanning optical microscope|Optical Scanning Microscopy]] (NSOM).<ref>Dressler, D. H.; Landau, A.; Zaban, A.; Mastai, Y., Sub-micrometer polarimetry of chiral surfaces using near-field scanning optical microscopy. Chemical Communications 2007, (9), 945-947.</ref> (5) [[Isothermal Titration Calorimetry]] (ITC)<ref>Shval, A.; Mastai, Y., Isothermal titration calorimetry as a new tool to investigate chiral interactions at crystal surfaces. Chemical Communications 47, (20), 5735-5737.</ref> for the determination of Nanoscale Chirality.

He has over 200 peer-reviewed articles in print, which were cited nearly 9,000 times. Mastai has published many book chapters and edited 3 books<ref>"Advances in Crystallization Processes", Editor Yitzhak Mastai, {{ISBN|978-953-51-0581-7}}, Publisher: InTech, August 2012.</ref><ref>Materials Science - Advanced Topics”, Editor Yitzhak Mastai, {{ISBN|978-953-51-1140-5}}, 560 pages, Publisher: InTech, Chapters published June 2013.</ref><ref>“Advanced Topics in Crystallization” ”, Editor Yitzhak Mastai, {{ISBN|978-953-51-2125-1}}, 370 pages Publisher: InTech, Chapters published May 2015.</ref> on various aspects of [[nanomaterials]] and [[materials science]].

Among his previous awards were the Minerva Postdoctoral Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.minerva.mpg.de/fellowships/fellowships.html |title=The Minerva Fellowship Program |access-date=2018-05-26 |archive-date=2018-05-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527023524/http://www.minerva.mpg.de/fellowships/fellowships.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> which he received in 2000 and the [[:he:מלגת אלון|Yigal Alon fellowship]] in 2003, for outstanding young researchers of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Israel Academy for higher education]]. Prof. Mastai served as Chairman of the Chemistry Department at Bar-Ilan University,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ch.biu.ac.il/ |title=Department of Chemistry, Bar Ilan University |access-date=2018-05-26 |archive-date=2021-11-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128170239/https://ch.biu.ac.il/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> between 2014 and 2017. 
He also served as an executive board member of the Israel Chemical Society (ICS),<ref>[http://www.chemistry.org.il/ Israel Chemical Society (ICS)]</ref> The Israel Vacuum Society (IVS),<ref>[http://www.ivs.org.il/ The Israel Vacuum Society (IVS)]</ref> the editorial board of the Journal of Nanomaterials<ref>[https://www.hindawi.com/journals/jnm/ Journal of Nanomaterials]</ref> and the Israel Journal of Chemistry (IJC).<ref>[https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/18695868 Israel Journal of Chemistry (IJC)]</ref>
